clue.text: Whip-round? I go silent

indicators.note: round asks for the whip word to be turned about, read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone asked to contribute to an office collection simply clams up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' looks like a collection of money, but it splits into a whip and a reversal signal. The definition 'silent' hides at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reticent who says little is described this way; it is a synonym of uncommunicative.

clue.text: Award put Helen initially in her place

indicators.note: in puts the initial letters inside the place name

parts.note: Helen of Troy, so her place is the city of Troy

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of put and of Helen

explanation.surface: An award puts Helen back in her home city.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or prize given to a winner.

clue.text: Cheap restaurant offering a hundred free spirit

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a hippy is a free-spirited nonconformist

explanation.surface: A budget eatery hands out a hundred free drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang for a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a fish-and-chip shop, an inexpensive takeaway.

clue.text: Boost, given termination of employment postponed shortly

indicators.note: termination of takes the final letter of employment
shortly cuts the last letter from the postponed phrase

parts.note: on ice means postponed or held in reserve

explanation.surface: Being told your notice is delayed gives a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims ON ICE to ONIC; T comes from the end of 'employment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up or stimulant that gives a lift.

clue.text: Nuclear device in race to explode rock

indicators.note: to explode means the letters of race are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or rock outcrop

explanation.surface: A nuclear plant in a race to blow up a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparatus in which a controlled chain reaction takes place.

clue.text: Horses here? Sure!

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the horses are kept here and gets a cheerful yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses are housed in a stable building; and stable also means steady or secure, as sure footing is.

clue.text: Two prizes lifted, being of the highest quality

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a reward is a prize
a pot is a prize, as in a sports cup

explanation.surface: Two awards carried off, being of the finest quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses REWARD POT as a whole, reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for first-class, from the best things being kept in the uppermost drawer.

clue.text: Soup given in blessing round university, bad

indicators.note: round means the blessing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a boon is a blessing
ill means bad

explanation.surface: Soup served at a university grace is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear broth made by simmering meat or vegetables.

clue.text: All English really on drug

parts.note: very means truly or really
E is slang for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: The whole English nation is genuinely on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Every person, the whole lot.

clue.text: Relation staggering from a long way off

indicators.note: staggering suggests lurching about, so the letters of relation are jumbled

explanation.surface: A family member reels in after travelling from distant parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern, from Asia, was a far-off place to the Europeans who coined the word.

clue.text: Tree far from gone to seed?

explanation.surface: A tree that is anything but neglected and overgrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer of the pine family; also an adjective meaning neat and smart in appearance, the opposite of shabby.

clue.text: Bone in vice round hospital

indicators.note: round puts the vice word around the hospital letter

parts.note: a sin is a vice
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A bone gripped in a vice in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The front of the leg below the knee, along the tibia.

clue.text: Game for drink after dance

indicators.note: after places the drink word behind the dance word in the answer

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: Someone plays a game to win a whisky once the dancing is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground pastime of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Get better given series of strokes

explanation.surface: A tennis player recovers form during a long exchange of shots.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover strength after illness or a slump; in tennis, a sustained exchange of shots.

clue.text: Small, average box

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
par is the normal or average level

explanation.surface: A small, middling box or crate.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice with a partner.

clue.text: Take off in long sort of suit

indicators.note: in puts the take-off word inside the longing word

parts.note: to long for is to pine
to strip is to take clothes off

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to undress from a particular suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit cloth with fine vertical lines, typical of City bankers.

clue.text: Loose women working, monthly occurrence

indicators.note: loose suggests letters set free to rearrange, so women is jumbled

parts.note: on means functioning or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Women of easy virtue at work once a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests women of easy virtue; 'Loose' is only the anagram signal, and 'working' gives its usual crossword sense of switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar phase when the moon is unlit recurs about every twenty-nine days.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink a failure in producing gymnastic feat

parts.note: a flip is a drink of beaten egg with spirit or wine
a flop is a failure

explanation.surface: A drink proves a disaster in a gymnastic routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A backward handspring, a tumbling move in gymnastics.

clue.text: Feign illness in arm and leg, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Faking illness by claiming a bad arm and leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk work by pretending to be sick.

clue.text: Latin made erudite

parts.note: made, as in made money, means earned

explanation.surface: Studying Latin has turned someone into a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person with deep scholarly knowledge.

clue.text: Swindle taking mum's money

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them
mum means silent, and sh is the call for hush

explanation.surface: A con trick that takes a mother's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for cash.

clue.text: Linesman in grey going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the grey word is written backwards

parts.note: drab means dull and grey

explanation.surface: A football official in a grey kit runs off in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' looks like a football official; here it is a man of lines, a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet writes lines of verse, so is cryptically a man of lines.

clue.text: Medication as the Rolling Stones, perhaps, get older

parts.note: the Rolling Stones are an example of a rock band
to age is to get older

explanation.surface: Ageing rock stars need their medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of material wrapped round a wound as a dressing.

clue.text: Show-off rose up in play

indicators.note: in play means the letters are set moving and rearranged

explanation.surface: A preening actor has risen in a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who acts affectedly to impress others.

clue.text: What's washed up in streams before twelve

parts.note: jets are streams of liquid
am means before midday

explanation.surface: Debris carried ashore by currents before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods thrown overboard that drift ashore.

clue.text: Run off, getting the runs during drink

indicators.note: during puts the runs letter within the drink word

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone dashes away with an upset stomach in the middle of a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off copies is to produce them on a press.

clue.text: Country unhappy about popular Gulf

indicators.note: about means the unhappy word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or unhappy
in means fashionable or popular
a gulf is a gap or chasm

explanation.surface: A nation is upset about a well-liked stretch of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A city-state in Southeast Asia, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: A lump which is positive

parts.note: a node is a lump or swelling

explanation.surface: A lump found to be a malignant positive.
explanation.definitionFit: The positively charged electrode of an electrolytic cell.

clue.text: Part of the theatre finds record good with perfect backing

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: backing means the perfect word is written backwards

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-rate or perfect

explanation.surface: A theatre box is found to have a fine record and perfect support.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-sided gallery, which in a theatre can be a box or balcony area.

clue.text: Noble to have singles in pubs

indicators.note: in places the singles word inside the pubs word

parts.note: bars are pubs
ones are single units

explanation.surface: An aristocrat drinks single measures in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress, a titled member of the nobility.

clue.text: One bearing cases of drink

explanation.surface: Someone carrying crates of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel or station worker carries luggage; also a dark beer brewed from roasted malt.

clue.text: Message from Mrs Simpson allowed to be sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: Marge is Mrs Simpson in the cartoon The Simpsons
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A note from Wallis Simpson that may be returned to sender.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Simpson suggests Wallis Simpson; it is the cartoon wife Marge. 'to be sent back' reverses MARGELET as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A wired communication sent through a telegraph office.
